Somerville.narrative: Somerville's real estate market remains one of the most competitive in Greater Boston, with single-family homes commanding a staggering median of $1,925,000 and selling at 103% of list price — with 57% of those homes closing above asking. Condos are equally active, with 47 units moving in the past 30 days at a median of $940,100 and 42.6% selling over list, while multi-families are fetching a median of $1,558,000 at 101.1% of list price with over half trading above ask. Inventory is essentially nonexistent across all property types, meaning buyers must come armed with strong pre-approvals, waived contingencies, and escalation clauses just to be competitive. For sellers, conditions couldn't be more favorable — properly priced Somerville properties are generating multiple offers almost immediately, making this an exceptional moment to maximize return on any asset class.

Cambridge.narrative: Cambridge continues to command some of the most competitive prices in Greater Boston, with single-family homes closing at a median of $2,550,000 and nearly half of all properties — 47.1% — selling above asking price across both single-family and condo segments. Condos remain a relatively more accessible entry point at a $929,500 median, yet with 63 units sold in the past 30 days and a 46.0% over-ask rate, buyers should expect to move quickly and come in with strong, clean offers. Multi-family properties are trading at $2,175,000 with a near-perfect 99.7% sale-to-list ratio, reflecting steady investor and owner-occupant demand for Cambridge's income-producing assets. With months of supply effectively at zero across all property types, sellers hold decisive leverage right now, while buyers need to be thoroughly pre-approved, prepared to waive contingencies, and realistic about the likelihood of bidding wars in virtually every price range.

Medford.narrative: Medford's real estate market is firing on all cylinders, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $788,000 and an impressive 100.7% sale-to-list ratio — 60% of those homes sold above asking price in the last 30 days. Condos closed at a median of $724,500 and multi-families commanded $1.2 million, with both property types hitting exactly list price on average and roughly 44-46% of sales going over ask. With effectively zero months of supply across all three property types and a combined 52 sales closed in the past 30 days, inventory is being absorbed as fast as it hits the market. Sellers are in a commanding position and can expect strong offers quickly, while buyers should come pre-approved, prepared to move decisively, and ready to compete — often without contingencies — to land a home in this high-demand, supply-starved city just minutes from Boston.

Melrose.narrative: Melrose's single-family market is firing on all cylinders, with a median sale price of $1,007,500 and a staggering 108.4% sale-to-list ratio — meaning buyers are routinely paying well above asking, with 75% of homes selling over list price across 28 transactions in the last 30 days. The near-zero months of supply tells you everything you need to know: inventory is essentially nonexistent, giving sellers extraordinary leverage and forcing buyers to come armed with aggressive offers and minimal contingencies. Condos are considerably more accessible at a $479,000 median with a 100% SP/LP ratio, though the thin sample of just 3 sales makes that segment harder to read with confidence. Sellers in Melrose, particularly single-family owners, are sitting in one of the strongest positions in Greater Boston right now, while buyers should expect multiple-offer situations and be prepared to stretch meaningfully beyond the asking price to secure a home.

Arlington.narrative: Arlington's single-family market is firing on all cylinders, with a median sale price of $1,338,500 and an average of 105.2% sale-to-list — meaning buyers are routinely paying well above asking, as evidenced by nearly 72% of homes selling over list price across 32 transactions in the last 30 days. Condos remain highly competitive as well, with a median of $860,000 and 39% of units closing above asking, though the slightly softer 98.8% SP/LP ratio suggests buyers have a touch more room to negotiate compared to the single-family segment. Multi-families tell a different story, with only 2 sales recorded, a median of $1,175,000, and a 94.4% SP/LP ratio with zero properties selling over ask — indicating investors are exercising more caution and holding firm on price discipline. Across all property types, the absence of meaningful months of supply signals an extraordinarily tight inventory environment, so sellers remain firmly in the driver's seat, while buyers — especially those targeting single-families — should expect to bring strong offers with limited contingencies to compete.

Belmont.narrative: Belmont's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $1,975,000 and a remarkable 77.8% of homes selling over asking price at 102.8% of list price — a clear signal that well-priced properties are triggering aggressive bidding wars. Condos are no slouch either, with a median of $910,000 and 55.6% selling above ask, while multi-families closed at a median of $1,078,969 with a slightly softer but still competitive 98.5% sale-to-list ratio. With effectively zero months of supply across all three categories and only 9 single-family and 9 condo sales in the past 30 days, inventory is critically tight, giving sellers exceptional leverage to command premium prices. Buyers should expect to move quickly, come in strong above list price — especially for single-family homes — and have financing buttoned up before stepping foot through the door.

Watertown.narrative: Watertown's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $1,175,000 and a remarkable 80% of properties selling over asking price at 101.1% of list price — a clear signal that buyers are entering bidding wars on nearly every available home. Condos offer a comparatively more accessible entry point at a $751,000 median, though 43.8% still closed above list at exactly 100% SP/LP on average, suggesting strong but slightly less frenzied demand. Multi-families commanded a $1,155,000 median with only 25% selling over ask and a 98% SP/LP ratio, indicating investors have marginally more negotiating room — though with just 4 sales in 30 days, inventory is razor-thin. With no measurable months of supply across any segment, sellers hold overwhelming leverage right now, while buyers should expect to move quickly, waive contingencies strategically, and come in above list price to have a realistic chance of landing a home in this inner-suburb market.

Winchester.narrative: Winchester's single-family market is commanding serious attention, with a median sale price of $2,362,500 and homes selling at 99% of list price — 35.7% of them closing above asking — across 14 sales in the past 30 days, all against a near-zero inventory backdrop that signals an extraordinarily tight supply. The condo segment is equally competitive, with a $795,500 median and a striking 50% of units selling over list price at 99.5% SP/LP, meaning even the attached-home market offers buyers little room to negotiate. The lone multi-family sale hit exactly $1,060,000 at 100% of list price, suggesting sellers are pricing with precision in that niche. For buyers, Winchester demands pre-approval, swift decision-making, and strong offers out of the gate; for sellers, this is an exceptional moment to list, as the lack of measurable months of supply means well-priced homes are effectively being absorbed as fast as they hit the market.

Boston.narrative: Boston's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a $925,000 median sale price and an eye-popping 102.6% sale-to-list ratio — meaning buyers are routinely bidding above asking, with 67.1% of single-family homes closing over list price in the past 30 days. The condo market, which saw the highest transaction volume with 342 sales, is comparatively more measured with a $799,500 median and only 26% of units selling over ask, though a 99.1% SP/LP ratio still signals very little negotiating room. Multi-families are holding firm at a $1,112,500 median with 44.2% selling above list, making them a sought-after investment play in a city where inventory is essentially nonexistent across all segments. For sellers, conditions couldn't be more favorable — the lack of measurable months supply means your home is likely to attract multiple offers quickly — while buyers should come prepared with strong pre-approvals, escalation clauses, and realistic expectations that list price is often just the starting point.
